golden: A condition is a ratio, a comparison and a value, like ROE > 15.
Each new line is a separate condition, and a company must match every line (the lines are joined with AND).
AND and OR join conditions on one line (&& and || also work). AND is applied before OR; brackets ( ) group them. A line that starts with AND or OR continues the line above.
Capital letters, extra spaces and everyday names (ROE, P/E, mcap, market cap) are read the same way. Start typing a name and the box suggests the real ones.
A bare number is read in the ratio's own unit: Market cap in ₹ crore, ROE in %. A unit may be written after it: 500 Cr, 15%, 15x, 30 days, 1 lakh crore.
Yes/no ratios are compared with yes or no: Pays a dividend = yes.
A company with no figure for a ratio in a condition does not match that condition. Companies left out only for that reason are counted under the results.
A query can hold up to 2,000 characters and 30 conditions. A ratio above your plan is marked with the plan that opens it.

syntax.meaning: Greater than, at least, less than, at most.
Equal to, not equal to. Equal means equal as shown: ROCE = 15 matches 15.04.
Inside a range, both ends included.
At least one condition must match.
Groups conditions, so an OR is applied before the AND next to it.
syntax.example: (P/E < 12 OR ROCE > 25) AND Debt to equity < 1

syntax.meaning: Joins the line above and below with AND.
Arithmetic between ratios and numbers. Both sides must be in the same unit.
A ratio can be compared with another ratio.
Amounts in ₹ crore. 1 lakh crore is 1,00,000 crore.
Digits with one decimal point, Indian grouping (1,00,000) and a minus sign are accepted.
Averages and growth periods are part of the ratio name.

notSupported: NOT. Turn the comparison round instead: P/E >= 15 in place of NOT P/E < 15, or use !=.
Sector, industry and index lists. A query compares ratios and numbers only; the Screener has those filters.
Quotes, commas, semicolons and comments. Write the name as it is and join conditions with AND, OR or a new line.

dos.why: Market cap is in ₹ crore: the long number reads as a very large amount, and a warning appears.
Conditions are joined with AND, OR or a new line, not a comma.
A condition compares two things. A range uses between, or two conditions with AND.
Yes/no ratios take = yes or = no.
Units are written as %, Cr, x or days.
ROE is already a percentage, so 0.15 means 0.15%. A warning appears.
Two conditions on one line need AND or OR between them.
A unit has to fit the ratio: market cap is an amount, not a percentage.

examples.title: Conditions on one line
examples.query: P/E < 15 AND Debt to equity < 1 AND ROE > 12

examples.title: OR inside brackets
examples.query:
(P/E < 12 OR Profit growth 5 years > 15)
Debt to equity < 1

examples.title: A range with between
examples.query:
ROE between 12 and 20
Market cap between 1000 Cr and 5000 Cr

examples.title: Small, low debt, high return
examples.query: Market cap < 5000 Cr AND Debt to equity < 0.5 AND ROCE > 18

examples.title: Growth over a period
examples.query:
Sales growth 5 years > 12
Profit growth 5 years > 10

empty.rule: A query needs at least one condition.
empty.fix: Type a condition such as ROE > 15, or insert one of the examples.

bad_character.rule: Only letters, numbers, comparisons, brackets and the units are used. Semicolons, quotes and similar characters are not part of the language.
bad_character.fix: Join conditions with AND, OR or a new line, and write ratio names without quotes.

bad_number.rule: A number has digits and at most one decimal point. Indian grouping such as 1,00,000 is accepted.
bad_number.fix: Write the number as 12.5 or 1,00,000, and put % after a number.

extra_paren.rule: Every ) closes a ( that was opened before it.
extra_paren.fix: Remove the extra ) or add the missing (.

missing_paren.fix: Add a ) where the group ends.

empty_paren.rule: Brackets hold at least one condition or value.
empty_paren.fix: Put a condition between the brackets or remove them.

missing_connector.rule: Two conditions on one line are joined with AND or OR. On separate lines, AND is implied.
missing_connector.fix: Insert AND or OR between them, or start a new line.

double_connector.rule: AND and OR each sit between two conditions.
double_connector.fix: Remove the extra word or put a condition between them.

dangling_connector.rule: AND and OR need a condition after them.
dangling_connector.fix: Add the next condition or remove the AND / OR.

starts_with_connector.rule: AND and OR need a condition before them.
starts_with_connector.fix: Put a condition before it, or remove it.

chained_comparison.rule: A condition compares two things. Two comparisons in a row are not read as a range.
chained_comparison.fix: Use between, or two conditions joined by AND.

between_and.rule: between takes two values joined by AND.

incomplete_condition.rule: A condition is a ratio, a comparison and a value.
incomplete_condition.fix: Add the comparison and the value, or = yes / = no for a yes/no ratio.

missing_operator.rule: A ratio and a value are separated by a comparison: >, <, >=, <=, = or !=.

missing_value.rule: A comparison has a number or another ratio after it.
missing_value.fix: Type the value after the comparison.

missing_metric.rule: A condition starts with a ratio name.
missing_metric.fix: Put a ratio name before the comparison.

unknown_metric.rule: Only ratios from the list can be used; a name that is not on it is not guessed. Matching ignores capitals, spaces and punctuation.
unknown_metric.fix: Pick the closest ratio, or open the full list of ratios.

bad_unit.rule: After a number the units are %, Cr (crore), lakh crore, x (times) and days.
bad_unit.fix: Use one of those units or no unit.

unit_mismatch.rule: The unit written on a number has to fit the ratio, and two sides of a comparison have to be in the same unit.
unit_mismatch.fix: Write the number in the ratio's unit, or drop the unit.

flag_operator.rule: Yes/no ratios are compared with = or !=.

flag_value.rule: A yes/no ratio is compared with yes or no (or 1 or 0).

yes_no_misuse.rule: yes and no work with yes/no ratios only.
yes_no_misuse.fix: Use a number with this ratio.

no_metric.rule: A condition uses at least one ratio; two plain numbers give the same answer for every company.
no_metric.fix: Compare a ratio with a number.

divide_by_zero.rule: A division by the plain number 0 has no answer.
divide_by_zero.fix: Divide by a non-zero number or by a ratio.

too_many_conditions.rule: A query can hold up to 30 conditions.
too_many_conditions.fix: Remove some, or split them into two baskets.

too_long.rule: A query can hold up to 2,000 characters.
too_long.fix: Shorten it, or split it into two baskets.

plan_locked.rule: Each ratio belongs to a plan, and a query can use the ratios of the member's own plan.
plan_locked.fix: Pick another ratio, or open the plan that includes it.

plan_score.rule: Each plan has one score: Gold and up use FinLit Prism, Silver the FinLit IQ. A Gold query never uses the FinLit IQ.
plan_score.fix: Use the plan's own score: Prism score and its parts on Gold, FinLit IQ and its parts on Silver.

unexpected.rule: After a condition comes a new line, AND, OR or the end of the query. A comma is not a joiner.
unexpected.fix: Replace the comma or stray word with AND, OR or a new line.

crore_units.rule: Amounts such as market cap, sales and profit are counted in ₹ crore.
crore_units.fix: Type the amount in crore: 5,000 for ₹5,000 crore.

looks_like_fraction.rule: Percentages are typed as percentages: 15 means 15%.

contradiction.rule: Conditions joined by AND must all be true together.
contradiction.fix: Join them with OR, or swap the numbers.

not.rule: NOT is not part of the language, so the word is read as a ratio name.
not.fix: Turn the comparison round: P/E >= 15 in place of NOT P/E < 15, or use !=.

text.rule: Sector, industry and index lists are not part of the query language. A query compares ratios and numbers.
text.fix: Remove the condition and use the sector or index filter in the Screener.

results: A company whose figure is missing is not listed for that condition, and the results say how many companies were left out only for that reason.
A loss-making company has no P/E, and a company with negative equity has no P/B, so conditions on those never match it. Growth from a negative base is also not a number.
Other negative values are compared as numbers: ROE > -5 includes a company at -2.
Show only recent results keeps the matches that have already reported the latest quarter; the others are counted and set aside.
Ratios above your plan are marked with the plan that opens them, and a query using one shows a message before it runs. The Basic plan lists the first 25 matches.
